headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: transformers can write/run shells and browsers while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, creating a dangerous shared-pipeline pair if connected.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, transformers can read/write files and run browsers, while nuwa-skill can emit allowlisted network egress; if an operator bridges them via files or copy-paste, raw content could be misread as instructions. This is a plausible but non-default pathway.
conditions: IF the operator passes transformers output into nuwa-skill via files or copy-paste
IF browser-sourced content is treated as instructions by the downstream workflow
mitigations: Use a plain-text handoff template
Strip markup before transfer
Require human review of any browser-derived text
Keep the agents on separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: transformers touches multimodal data and has broad filesystem/network surfaces, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or file handoff, sensitive content processed by transformers can flow into nuwa-skill outputs or outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style document workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file tree
IF transformers processes sensitive documents before nuwa-skill sends derived content outbound
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable outbound calls for sensitive runs
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Log and review all outbound destinations
Use a one-way export file with minimal fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: transformers has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, browser, and broad egress, while nuwa-skill has network egress and is verified as runnable. If both operate on the same mutable resources, concurrent writes or conflicting side effects can corrupt files or produce irrecoverable state. Uncertainty is limited because the overlap is explicit in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or serialization
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks
Mount shared paths read-only
Snapshot the workspace before execution

D_cascading_error.rationale: transformers can generate or transform content that nuwa-skill may then use in a pipeline, and nuwa-skill has outbound egress. If downstream logic treats upstream output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect external actions. The pair is not documented as integrated, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes transformers output without validation
IF the downstream step uses that output to make external requests or decisions
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require schema validation on handoff data
Add confidence thresholds before actioning outputs
Keep a human approval gate for external actions
Record provenance for each transferred artifact

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both are open-source docs-only profiles. The only concrete compliance-relevant surface is transformers' broad data handling and nuwa-skill's allowlisted egress, which could matter if regulated data is introduced, but that is not established here.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through transformers and then exported by nuwa-skill
IF the deployment imposes residency or retention rules not reflected in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Document retention and export paths
Review outbound allowlists
Add a data-class policy check
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
